h1: The 7 Best Upright Vacuums for Hardwood Floors, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Hardwood Floor Uprights: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 upright vacuums for hardwood floors from Sebo, Shark, Kenmore and Eureka, scored on floor control, weight, bins and pet use.
summary: The Sebo 9855AM Dart is the upright to buy for hardwood floors if you want precise control and a long motor warranty. The Sebo Automatic X4 is the cheaper route to the same brand, while the Shark NV752 Rotator suits homes with both hardwood and carpet. The Kenmore Featherlite and Eureka Airspeed are the light, budget choices for smaller homes.
intro: The upright vacuum is the wrong tool for hardwood unless it can stop spinning its brush. A beater bar designed for carpet flicks debris across a bare floor, chatters over board gaps and, with the wrong bristles, leaves fine scratches in the finish. Many uprights advertise hardwood on the box and then make the buyer find out about the brush the hard way.

So this ranking looks at how each upright behaves on a bare floor, not just how hard it sucks. We reviewed seven models from their listings, comparing brand design, weight class, bin type, filtration and pet claims. The listings are thin on technical details such as brush shutoff, so we flag what to check on the product page before you click buy.

products.name: Sebo 9855AM Dart Upright Vacuum Cleaner with 7-Year Motor Warranty
products.verdict: Precise hard-floor control from a brand that backs its motor for seven years.
products.description:
The Sebo 9855AM Dart is a premium upright from a German maker, listed with a 7-year motor warranty and priced above $500. It is the pick for buyers who want exact control on hard floors.

It tops the ranking because the brand has built a reputation for bagged uprights that handle mixed flooring without scattering dust, and the motor warranty shows how confident the maker is. A long warranty on the part that fails most often is the clearest sign of build quality in this list. Bagged designs also hold dust inside until you toss the bag, which keeps fine hardwood dust out of the air.

Buy it if you plan to keep the vacuum for a decade and want precision on bare wood. The price is the main hurdle, and the listing gives few specifications, so read the product page for brush control and weight.
products.idealFor: Owners of real hardwood who want a vacuum for ten years.
products.skipIf: You need to keep spending under $200.

products.name: Sebo Automatic X4 Upright Vacuum Cleaner
products.verdict: The longest-running Sebo upright, reliable on hardwood and priced lower than the Dart.
products.description:
The Sebo Automatic X4 is a long-standing upright in the brand's lineup, listed in the $500+ bucket. The name refers to automatic height adjustment, which lets the head adapt as you move between rug and floor.

It ranks second because it brings the same brand philosophy at a more approachable price, and the automatic adjustment is valuable in homes that mix hardwood and area rugs. Having the head follow the floor means fewer manual settings. It trails the Dart on stated warranty, since the listing doesn't mention a motor term, and on the finer control the Dart's listing highlights.

Choose it if you want reliable hardwood performance without paying top dollar. The caveat is that it is still a premium purchase compared with the mainstream Shark and Kenmore options.
pros: Head adapts between floors and rugs
products.idealFor: Homes with hardwood and rugs together.
products.skipIf: You want the longest motor warranty.

products.name: Sebo Essential G5 Upright Vacuum Cleaner 90407AM Light & Dark Grey
products.verdict: A lighter-spec Sebo for shoppers weighing a premium upright against mainstream brands.
products.description:
The Sebo Essential G5 (90407AM) comes in light and dark grey and sits in the $500+ bucket. It is the more basic model in the Sebo range here.

It ranks third because the listing offers little beyond the brand and the model number, and it is described as suited to buyers comparison shopping. The Sebo name still carries weight on hardwood, where careful floor handling matters more than raw suction. Against the X4 and Dart it gives up some premium touches.

Buy it if you want the Sebo approach on a tighter budget. Skip it if you want the best-supported Sebo, since the other two models carry stronger listings.
cons: Premium price for a basic model
products.idealFor: Buyers who want Sebo quality on a tighter budget.
products.skipIf: You want a long stated warranty.

products.name: Shark NV752 Rotator Powered Lift-Away TruePet Upright Vacuum with HEPA Filter, Large Dust Cup Capacity, LED Headlights, Upholstery Tool, Perfect Pet Power Brush & Crevice Tool, Bordeaux
products.verdict: A lift-away upright with HEPA, LED headlights and a large cup, for homes with hardwood and carpet.
products.description:
Shark's NV752 Rotator is a powered lift-away upright that bundles HEPA filtration, big dust cup capacity, LED headlights and a trio of pet, upholstery and crevice tools. Expect to spend $200 to $500.

It lands fourth because it is the most versatile machine here for a house with mixed floors. The lift-away design lets you detach the pod for stairs and furniture, and LED headlights show dust along baseboards that a normal room light hides. The HEPA filter suits allergy households. The tradeoff is that Shark's core strength is carpet, so check that the brushroll can be switched off before running it on bare wood.

Choose it for a home with mostly carpet and some hardwood. Skip it if hardwood is nearly everywhere.
products.idealFor: Mixed hardwood and carpet homes with pets.
products.skipIf: Almost every room is bare hardwood.

products.name: Shark Navigator Lift-Away Vacuum, HEPA, Pet Hair, White/Silver, NV356E
products.verdict: A popular lift-away Shark with HEPA and pet-hair credentials, in the $100 to $200 bracket.
products.description:
The Shark Navigator Lift-Away (NV356E) in white and silver carries a HEPA filter and a pet-hair focus, and costs $100 to $200. It is a bagless lift-away upright.

It lands fifth because pet hair on hardwood is a daily chore, and a vacuum with a lift-away pod and a sealed-ish filter system makes it easier to reach under furniture. The model is among the best-known Shark uprights, so parts and accessories are easy to find. The limit is that it is a mainstream carpet-minded design, and hardwood users need to confirm the brush can be disabled.

Buy it if you have pets and a mix of surfaces on a mid-range budget. Skip it if hardwood is the main surface and you can afford a Sebo.
products.idealFor: Pet owners with mixed floors on a mid-range budget.
products.skipIf: Hardwood is the only surface in your home.

products.name: Kenmore Featherlite Lift-Up Bagless Upright Vacuum
products.verdict: A light bagless upright that is easy to push and carry, in the $100 to $200 bracket.
products.description:
The Kenmore Featherlite Lift-Up is a bagless upright built around low weight and a lift-up design, selling for $100 to $200.

Sixth place comes down to the fact that light weight is a genuine benefit on hardwood. A heavy upright pushes into floors and is awkward on stairs, while a light one glides and carries easily. It is a good partner for apartment living. The compromise is that bagless uprights at this price tend to be loud and less durable than a Sebo, and the listing lacks detail about brush control.

Buy it if weight is your priority. Skip it if you need a quiet or highly durable machine.
products.idealFor: People who struggle with heavy vacuums.
products.skipIf: You want a long-lasting premium upright.

products.name: Eureka Vacuum Cleaners for Home,Airspeed Ultra-Lightweight, NEU10AE5
products.verdict: The cheapest and lightest upright here, aimed at smaller homes.
products.description:
The Eureka Airspeed NEU10AE5 is an ultra-lightweight upright in the $50 to $100 bucket and is pitched at smaller homes.

It ranks last because the low price tells you what to expect: lighter materials, fewer attachments and a shorter service life. For a small apartment with hardwood floors, that can be enough, since the weight makes it easy to use and store. It is also the lowest-risk purchase for someone who wants to try an upright without a big spend.

Buy it if your home is small and the budget is tight. Skip it if you have a large house or lots of pet hair.
products.skipIf: You have a large home or heavy shedding.

whatMatters.detail: A spinning brush on bare wood flicks debris and can scratch. The best uprights for hardwood let you switch the brush off or use a soft roller. Look in the product page for a brush on and off switch, since many listings leave it out.
Heavy uprights press into the floor and are tiring on stairs. Soft rubber wheels glide and avoid marks, hard plastic wheels can scuff. Check the stated weight and wheel type.

Bagged uprights seal dust inside until disposal, which keeps fine dust down. Bagless designs save on bags but need regular emptying and filter washing. Decide based on allergies and how you feel about bag costs.
A HEPA filter captures fine particles, which matters for allergies and for the dust that hardwood vacuuming stirs up. Check that the listing says HEPA and that the filter can be cleaned or replaced.
The motor is the part that costs the most to fix. A long motor warranty, such as the Sebo Dart's seven years, signals confidence. Check also that belts and filters are easy to buy.

cards.label: Bagged
cards.text: Dust stays sealed until you toss the bag, which helps allergies and keeps the air cleaner. Picks: the three Sebo uprights.

cards.label: Bagless
cards.text: No bag costs and you can see the dirt, but emptying releases dust and filters need washing. Picks: Shark NV752, NV356E, Kenmore Featherlite and Eureka Airspeed.

howToChoose.note: Default to bagged if anyone in the home has allergies, and bagless if you want to avoid ongoing bag costs.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A brush you can turn off, a tool for pet hair on furniture and stairs, and HEPA filtration for dander. Wide floor heads with soft edges help avoid scratches.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Shark Navigator NV356E and Shark NV752 TruePet for pet-specific tools, or the Sebo Dart for the best hard-floor control.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Your floors are real hardwood you want to protect, or you plan to keep the vacuum a decade. The Sebo Dart and X4 are built for that.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: The floors are laminate or you have a small space. The Eureka Airspeed or Kenmore Featherlite will do.

faq.q: Can an upright vacuum scratch hardwood?
faq.a: It can if the brushroll is stiff or the wheels are hard plastic. Look for a model where you can turn the brush off, and keep the wheels and head clean of grit.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake with hardwood vacuums?
faq.a: Using a spinning beater bar on bare floors. It scatters debris and can scuff the finish. Always switch off the brush or choose a model made for hard floors.

faq.q: Is a Sebo worth it over a Shark?
faq.a: If hardwood is your main surface and you plan to keep it for years, yes. If you have mixed flooring and pets on a budget, a Shark offers more tools for less.

faq.q: How do I empty a bagless vacuum without a dust cloud?
faq.a: Empty it outdoors or into a trash bag held tightly around the canister. Tap gently and wash the filter on schedule so airflow stays strong.

faq.q: How often should I replace filters and belts?
faq.a: Check the manual, but filters usually need washing every few months and replacing yearly, and belts when they stretch or crack. Keep spares if the machine is your main vacuum.
Lift-away models like the Shark Navigator handle stairs best because you carry the pod. Heavy uprights like the Sebo are harder to use on stairs.

finalTake: The Sebo 9855AM Dart is the best upright for hardwood floors here, with precise control and a seven-year motor warranty. The Sebo Automatic X4 is the more affordable way into the brand, while the Shark NV752 and NV356E suit homes that mix hardwood with carpet and pets. Choose the Kenmore or Eureka if weight and price decide it, and always confirm the brush can be turned off.
